newsitem.title: USA: Gelman says committed to Memtec deal.
newsitem.headline: Gelman says committed to Memtec deal.

text.p: Gelman Sciences Inc said it remains committed to a planned $280-million stock acquisition by Australia's Memtec Ltd.

"Both of these companies are extremely committed to doing this deal," said Gelman president and chief operating officer Kim Davis in a conference call following release of the company's fourth-quarter financial results.
"Our fourth-quarter results are known to Memtec. They have high confidence in our ability to deliver on our fiscal 1997. I would say we're progressing solidly on schedule," he said.
Shares in Gelman were off 3/8 to 26-1/2.
The company reported a fourth-quarter loss of $0.25 per share, versus a $0.27 per share profit a year earlier.

Under their merger agreement, if the American depository shares of Memtec trade at an average price of less than $30 each over the 45-day period preceding the closing date, Gelman may walk away or renegotiate the deal.
Memtec American depository shares on Thursday were trading at about $27. Davis said he anticipates closing the merger in the first week of December.
Gelman business analysis manager Ivo Marcich said that would start the pricing period in mid-October.

Gelman makes microfiltration products for laboratories, healthcare, environmental monitoring, high-technology process industries and other uses. Memtec is also in the purification and separation business.
